problem.text: Linear previously rounded only output width. Input widths remained unpadded, and pad_out returned immediately when output padding was unnecessary.

reasoning.text: The change retains the original input width separately and rounds the operational width to pad_to, defaulting to 128. It extends weight padding to input-only cases without changing the forward method.

impact.text: The padded input width propagates to FP16 and EXL3 layer construction, Hessian allocation and weights_numel. Forward still delegates without explicitly padding activations, so compatible activation widths remain a caller-side requirement.

source_notes.text: Issue #8, “RuntimeError: shape '[5120, -1, 128]' is invalid for input of size 776524800,” reports vocabulary/output-padding failures and successful fixes before this task. Its relationship here is contextual inference based on the shared Linear conversion path and padding concern, not evidence that this input-padding change fixed that report.

Issue #7 reports an undefined-symbol import failure and an environment workaround; issue #15 reports incoherent Cogito output at bpw <= 2.5 and discusses regularization. Neither discussion establishes an input-padding cause.
The earlier slicing entry records padding-before-slicing and default CPU-staging concerns.

limitations: No PyTorch assignment, model loading, quantization or CUDA kernel was executed; the executed check models integer dimensions and slice shapes only.
End-to-end activation-width compatibility, memory cost and performance were not measured.
The inspected source establishes 128 as the existing padding default, not a universally sufficient alignment for every backend.

chapters.title: Extend linear weight padding to input channels

claims.text: For input-only padding, pad_out allocates an output-by-padded-input zero tensor and copies the original columns into its prefix. Existing output-only padding copies rows; one-dimensional biases retain output-width padding. Both ordinary and fused FP16 loading call this helper before constructing LinearFP16.

The rounding expression computes the smallest pad_to multiple not below the requested width. A standard-library transcription checked the default-128 invariant for widths 1–1024 and matching copy shapes for input-only and output-only examples.

Zero-filled added weight columns preserve the original contribution when inputs already have the corresponding expanded width. The tradeoff is a larger stored matrix; this helper does not itself expand activation tensors.

Inspection of the parent plus task diff shows that padding still precedes feature slicing, preserving the earlier slicing incompatibility. The default is_sliced comparison against optional None dimensions also remains unchanged.

findings.description: The output-padding branch prevents simultaneous input padding from copying into a correctly bounded destination.
findings.trigger: Load an ordinary 130-by-130 weight with default pad_to=128.
findings.expected_behavior: Copy into the leading 130-by-130 region of a zero-filled 256-by-256 matrix.
findings.actual_behavior: The output-width condition selects padded[:130, :], a 130-by-256 destination, for the 130-by-130 source; the input-column branch is skipped.

verification.description: Whole-parent literal searches locate pad_out calls only in ordinary and fused load_fp16 branches; Linear.load directly invokes load_fp16 after EXL3 lookup. The finding concerns weights needing both axes padded, not all model loads.
verification.limits: No model exhibiting these dimensions was executed.

verification.description: Computed the incompatible source and destination slice shapes.
verification.limits: Does not execute tensor assignment or establish its exact exception.

findings.description: The inherited full-weight padding-before-slicing incompatibility persists, with input padding now changing the destination width too.
findings.trigger: Load a full 512-by-64 weight while requesting 130 outputs and 64 inputs, full_out_features=512 and first_out_feature=0.
findings.expected_behavior: Select the requested feature region before padding the local matrix.
findings.actual_behavior: pad_out allocates 256-by-128 and attempts to copy the full 512-by-64 source before LinearFP16 can slice it.

verification.description: The ordinary FP16 loader still pads before constructing the slicing backend. Whole-parent search identifies Linear.load as its direct caller.
verification.limits: Reach is conditional on an explicit sliced request; no existing model construction with this request was demonstrated.

verification.description: Checked the full source and padded destination slice dimensions.

annotation.summary: Adds input-width rounding and input-only weight padding, but simultaneous two-axis padding remains incompatible and padding-before-slicing is unchanged.

argv:
p=lambda n:(n+127)//128*128
for i,o in [(130,256),(128,130),(130,130),(64,130)]:
 I,O=p(i),p(o)
 src=(512,i) if (i,o)==(64,130) else (o,i)
 dst=(min(src[0],O),I) if O!=o else (O,min(src[1],I))
 print({'input':i,'output':o,'padded':(O,I),'source':src,'copy_target':dst,'exact_shape_match':src==dst})
assert all(n<=p(n)<n+128 and p(n)%128==0 for n in range(1,1025))
print('round-up invariant passed for 1..1024')
